label: GO after unrewarded S2 trial, late episode, policy undecided; boosted if S1 rewarded before
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_trial * np.exp(-np.abs(choice)/2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == 2) * ep_trial * np.exp(-np.abs(choice)/2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial * np.exp(-np.abs(choice)/2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial * np.exp(-np.abs(choice)/2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 2)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.2% of steps) that fires only at GO. It is zero at D1 and D2. Its magnitude rises with episode trial: the timing baseline peaks in deciles 7-8. Given that, it is raised almost only when the previous trial reached S2 unrewarded. The rise is strongest after a1 S2 u (rare, unrewarded, where a model-based agent stays). It is weaker after a2 S2 u. It scales with ep_trial and is largest when the policy logit (choice) is near zero, i.e. the agent is undecided. It is boosted further when the trial before that was rewarded, more so if that trial reached S1. All other previous-trial patterns lower it slightly. Hidden good state, value and reward are not needed (value adds little). Scores (R^2 beyond timing): the prev S2-unrewarded indicator alone gives 0.03 (dev). Adding ep_trial x near-zero-choice weighting gives 0.10-0.12. Adding trial-before reward x state gives 0.177 dev and 0.166 test. That beats the profile all ceiling of 0.08 because of the multiplicative terms. Most variance comes from rare large spikes (0.7-0.95) that stay heavily under-predicted, so the magnitude is only weakly explained.
